courses.name: IT Remote Worker English
courses.description: Bahasa Inggris praktis untuk tim IT remote: stand-up singkat, pembaruan progres, code review, dan wawancara kerja. Mulai dari aktivitas mana pun dan belajar dengan tempo sendiri.
courses.label: Career English

categories.name: Remote work essentials
categories.label: Workplace listening
categories.guide: Listen for the task, deadline, and next action.

units.title: Daily stand-up update
units.subtitle: Catch the progress, blocker, and next step.

content.objective: Understand a concise remote-team status update.
content.script: Hi, everyone. I finished the new sign-in screen yesterday and opened a pull request this morning. I am waiting for a review from Sam before merging it. My only blocker is the test environment, which has been unavailable since nine. I will contact the platform team after this call. If it is ready by lunchtime, I can complete the integration tests today. Otherwise, I will update the project board and move that task to tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker finish yesterday?
questions.explain: The speaker says the new sign-in screen was finished yesterday.
The test environment has been unavailable since nine.

questions.prompt: What will the speaker do if the environment is not ready?
options: Update the project board and move the task
Ask Sam to complete the tests
questions.explain: The speaker will update the board and move the task to tomorrow.

categories.name: Remote team communication
categories.label: AI Lesson
categories.guide: Give a clear update, explain one detail, and invite a response.

units.title: Give a project update
units.subtitle: Explain what is done, what is next, and what is blocked.
units.masterPrompt: You are a calm English coach for remote IT professionals. Keep the learner's meaning, ask one focused follow-up, and correct only clear, useful English errors. Do not invent mistakes.

content.prompt: You are joining a short remote-team stand-up. Tell your teammates what you completed, what you will work on next, and whether anything is blocking you. Include one specific detail.
content.objective: Deliver a concise and natural status update in a remote team.

units.title: Discuss a code review
units.subtitle: Ask for clarification and respond constructively.
units.masterPrompt: Act as a supportive software teammate. Discuss the code review in English; never pretend the learner made an error that is not present.

content.prompt: A teammate has left a comment asking you to simplify a function. Explain your approach, ask one polite clarifying question, and suggest a next step.
content.objective: Use collaborative language during a code review.

categories.name: Live team conversations
categories.label: Live Lesson
categories.guide: Practice spontaneous conversations as a remote teammate.

units.title: Sprint planning call
units.subtitle: Agree priorities and negotiate a realistic task estimate.
units.masterPrompt: Guide a realistic sprint-planning role-play. Start speaking first and keep your colleague role friendly and concise.

content.teacherRole: a supportive software teammate facilitating sprint planning
content.learnerRole: a developer explaining capacity and choosing a sprint task
content.situation: Your remote team is planning a one-week sprint. The team has a small bug fix, a new feature, and a technical-debt task to prioritize.
content.opening: Good morning, everyone. Before we choose our sprint tasks, how much time do you have available this week?

courses.name: Tour Guide English
courses.description: Bahasa Inggris praktis untuk pemandu wisata: menyambut tamu, menjelaskan tempat bersejarah, memberi arahan, dan menjawab pertanyaan wisatawan.
courses.label: Tourism English

categories.name: Welcoming visitors
categories.label: Guided tour listening
categories.guide: Listen for meeting points, timings, and visitor questions.

units.title: Meet the group
units.subtitle: Listen for the departure time and meeting point.

content.objective: Identify key details in a tour welcome announcement.
content.script: Welcome to the old town walking tour. My name is Dina, and I will be your guide this morning. We will leave the visitor center at half past nine and walk to the central square. Please keep your ticket with you; we will check it before entering the museum. The walk takes about fifteen minutes, and there is a short stop for water along the way. If you have any questions or need a slower pace, please let me know.

questions.prompt: When does the group leave the visitor center?
questions.explain: The guide says the group leaves at half past nine.

questions.prompt: How long does the walk to the square take?
questions.explain: The walk takes about fifteen minutes.

questions.prompt: What should visitors keep with them?
questions.explain: The guide asks everyone to keep their ticket with them.

categories.name: Explain and recommend
categories.label: AI Lesson
categories.guide: Describe a place clearly and make visitors feel welcome.

units.title: Introduce a local attraction
units.subtitle: Create a short, engaging introduction for visitors.
units.masterPrompt: You are a friendly English coach for a local tour guide. Encourage accurate, vivid descriptions and never invent a learner error.

content.prompt: Imagine you are guiding visitors at a local attraction you know well. Welcome the group, describe one interesting feature, and explain why it matters. Finish by inviting one question.
content.objective: Give a warm, informative introduction to a place of interest.

units.title: Recommend local food
units.subtitle: Explain a dish and help a visitor choose.
units.masterPrompt: You are a considerate speaking coach. Ask about the visitor's preferences and help the learner explain local food clearly.

content.prompt: A visitor asks what local dish they should try. Recommend a dish, describe its main ingredients and taste, and mention one useful detail such as spice level or a dietary option.
content.objective: Explain a local food recommendation in a helpful way.

categories.name: Tourist conversations
categories.label: Live Lesson
categories.guide: Respond naturally to common visitor questions.

units.title: Help a visitor find a place
units.subtitle: Give clear directions and check that the visitor understands.
units.masterPrompt: Start as a visitor who needs directions. Keep turns short, be polite, and let the learner explain a route.

content.teacherRole: a friendly visitor exploring the town
content.learnerRole: a local tour guide giving directions
content.situation: The visitor wants to walk from the central square to a nearby traditional market and is unsure which street to take.
content.opening: Excuse me, I am trying to find the traditional market. Is it within walking distance from here?

ad.title: Make your next conversation count
ad.description: Practice practical English with short guided lessons and friendly conversation.
